URL: https://www.ipsos.com/en-uk/labour-now-lead-8-points-conservatives-second-place-latest-voting-intention-polling
Outlet: Ipsos, published 25.10.26 (fieldwork 15-22 October 2026, 1,109 British adults 18+)

Labour now lead by 8 points with the Conservatives in second place in latest voting intention polling

Key Voting Intention Figures
- Labour: 32% (+5 from September)
- Conservatives: 24% (+3)
- Reform UK: 20% (-3)
- Liberal Democrats: 9% (+1)
- Greens: 8% (-5)

This represents "the largest Labour lead with Ipsos - and first time we have seen the Conservatives in second place - since June 2025."

Government satisfaction stands at 23% (+5), with 66% dissatisfied. The net satisfaction score of -43 represents "the highest recorded since Boris Johnson was Prime Minister."

Regarding re-election, 30% believe the government deserves to be re-elected, while 47% disagree.

Leader Satisfaction Ratings
- Andy Burnham (PM): 35% satisfied (+4)
- Kemi Badenoch (Conservative leader): 35% satisfied (+7)
- Zack Polanski (Green leader): 17% satisfied (-1)
- Nigel Farage (Reform UK leader): 22% satisfied (-2)
- Ed Davey (Lib Dem leader): 20% satisfied (-3)

Readiness for Government
Only 19% believe Reform UK is ready to govern (down from 22% last month). For Conservatives, 24% think they're ready for government, up 4 points from the previous month.

Key Issues Analysis
On asylum and immigration, Reform UK leads Labour 28% to 14%. On healthcare, Labour leads the Conservatives by 16 points (27% to 11%). The economy shows Labour and Conservatives neck-and-neck at 20% versus 18%.

Keiran Pedley, Director of Politics at Ipsos, stated: "Whilst the headline figures do show a striking change, they confirm a pattern we have been seeing in the underlying data for some time."

He cautioned: "The Government faces a challenging budget this coming week and the lesson of the last year is the British politics is volatile."
